sources.name: WHO Fact Sheets
sources.use_for: Malaria, hypertension, diabetes, diet, physical activity, immunization, water, cholera.
sources.how: Open the fact sheet, rewrite the key facts in your own words, keep the entry source as 'WHO - <sheet name>'.

sources.name: CDC (US Centers for Disease Control)
sources.use_for: Conditions, prevention, vaccines, emergency warning signs.
sources.how: Search cdc.gov for the condition, use the prevention/symptoms section, cite 'CDC - <page>'.

sources.name: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine)
sources.use_for: Plain-language drug and condition pages (paracetamol, ibuprofen, diabetes).
sources.how: Use the topic page summary; cite 'MedlinePlus - <topic>'. Has MedlinePlus Connect API for coded lookup.

sources.name: NHS Conditions
sources.use_for: Sleep, hydration, handwashing, fever, paracetamol, ibuprofen, colds.
sources.how: Use the Conditions A-Z page, rewrite self-care steps, cite 'NHS - <page>'.

sources.name: OpenFDA (US FDA drug data)
sources.use_for: Structured drug labels and adverse events (JSON API, free, no key for basic use).
sources.how: Query api.fda.gov/drug/label.json e.g. ?search=openfda.brand_name:paracetamol. Store key facts + source 'OpenFDA - <drug>'.

sources.name: WHO ICD-11 Classification
sources.use_for: Coded disease names for condition field (e.g. malaria, hypertension codes).
sources.how: Look up the condition code, store it in the entry condition field. Needs a free token for API use.
